profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a software engineering research lab preparing the next two-week implementation sprint for an internal prototype that adds actionable planning support based on XTREE and BELLTREE to an existing software analytics platform. The team already has prediction dashboards for defect risk, and this meeting is to plan what will be built next so they can demo 'learning effective changes for software projects' to a sponsor at the end of the sprint. The agenda is to decide the scope of the prototype increment, how XTREE and BELLTREE plans will be generated and shown in the product, what data and environments will be used, who owns each workstream, and what counts as being demo-ready. The expected outcome is a shared implementation plan with task split, timeline, and a demo target for the sprint review.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: Product planning, analytics workflow design, stakeholder demos, translating research outputs into user-facing features
members.background: Former engineering manager who now leads product for an internal platform used by software quality teams; she has been coordinating with a sponsor who wants to see actionable recommendations, not just risk scores.
members.private_state: She wants a polished, low-risk demo that visibly closes the gap between prediction and planning, and she is trying to avoid last-minute integration surprises that could embarrass the team in front of the sponsor.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'prototype,' it means an end-to-end user-visible flow inside the existing analytics UI, even if some backend logic is simplified.
Using the 'Apache data' for the sprint means the cleaned cross-project benchmark package already used in prior sponsor demos, not raw project exports.
If a feature is 'demo-ready,' it should include stable-looking recommendations with explanatory text and no obvious failure cases during a guided walkthrough.
A 'plan' shown to users should be a concise recommended change set attached to a project snapshot, not a research artifact requiring parameter tuning.
Running something in 'staging' implies using the near-production web stack where PMs rehearse demos, not a notebook or service-only environment.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: Mining software repositories, experimental ML systems, implementing tree-based planning algorithms, evaluation pipelines
members.background: He joined from a software analytics research group and has implemented decision-tree-based recommenders before; he is responsible for turning the XTREE/BELLTREE papers into working internal services.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve technical credibility by implementing a faithful first version of the planning algorithms and avoid spending most of the sprint on UI polish instead of the core planner logic.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'prototype,' it means a functioning planner service plus minimal output wiring, with UI polish deferred until the algorithm behavior is validated.
Using the 'Apache data' means the latest mined repository snapshots and metrics he extracted from Apache projects last month for cross-project experiments.
If something is 'demo-ready,' it only needs to generate plausible plans on the selected dataset without errors in a controlled engineering run.
A 'plan' is the algorithmic delta between current metric ranges and recommended lower-risk ranges, which can initially be surfaced as raw feature adjustments.
Running in 'staging' can mean deploying the planner service to the shared pre-prod Kubernetes namespace and exercising it through internal endpoints, even without the full product UI.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to deliver 'the prototype' this sprint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means an end-to-end feature in the existing product where a user can open a project, click into recommendations, and see polished XTREE/BELLTREE plan cards suitable for a sponsor demo.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a backend planner implementation with basic API output and perhaps a simple internal viewer, with UI integration beyond minimal wiring postponed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In software teams, 'prototype' is a common term that often goes unexamined because both sides feel they are being pragmatic; each assumes the other shares the same obvious level of completeness.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Apache dataset is being used
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they will use 'the Apache data' for the sprint and the demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the cleaned benchmark dataset bundled in the analytics platform's demo workspace, based on older curated Apache project tables already approved for sponsor-facing screenshots.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of his newer mined Apache repository dataset with refreshed metrics and cross-project splits used in his recent BELLTREE experiments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both datasets are legitimately referred to inside the team as 'the Apache data,' and because the meeting is about planning rather than data science review, neither person expects they need to disambiguate which package is meant.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the sprint should 'support XTREE and BELLTREE recommendations.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the product should let a user see both within-project and cross-project recommendations available from the same project detail page, even if one is simplified behind the scenes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the planner service should implement both algorithms as supported modes, but only one mode needs to be actually exposed in the sprint flow while the other can exist as an offline run or hidden endpoint.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase names the same algorithms and sounds like shared support, but it leaves unstated whether support refers to user-facing availability, backend capability, or merely code-level inclusion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to have it 'demo-ready in staging by Thursday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means by Thursday afternoon the full user path in the staging web app should be reliable enough for rehearsal, with stable outputs, explanatory labels, and no manual intervention.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means by Thursday end of day the planner service should be deployed in the staging cluster and capable of producing recommendations through internal API calls for a controlled demo setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The team commonly uses deadlines with environment names as shorthand, and both interpretations are professionally reasonable; the gap hides inside different standards for what counts as sufficiently ready.
